asr.full_text: Hello everyone. Here is Max. And today we're talking about LuminLay. And let's begin with answering these two questions. What is LuminLay, and why would you need something like that. Well, apparently, it stands for luminescent inlay, or, in other words, glow in the dark thread markers. LuminLay is a Japanese product, and the website claims it to be the best of its kind. Well I'm not sure it that's provable, but anyway, this is a nice little feature to have. Like if you're on stage and a song begins in complete darkness. That kind of thing. I wanted to have something like this in my guitar, because why not? So i found this website, Lumenleuminley.com and there a quite a few different options here, two colors, a lot of different sizes, for the front of the fingerboard and side dots. There are even some glow-in-the-dark accessories for pedals. And any of that can be ordered directly from the website. The prices are in japanese Yen and for example for side dots 1800, 1,800 yuan make a little less than 14 euros or a little more than 16 US dollars. But this doesn't include shipping. Ok, there are more options here for the front of the fingerboard. Anglo in the dark thread lines for threadless instruments. There are also soo instructions here on how to install it and a list of brands who already used Lumenlei. You can see ESP, Mayonnaise Guitars, Strandberg, and some others. I've picked SB30 and got it from Ebay because for some reason it was more convenient for me than buying from the official website even though it was a little bit more expensive. Just for fun I've checked Facebook and turned out Lumen lay has a page with a lot of nice pictures and more than 9000 likes. Well, let's take a close look at the product. This is literally all I found inside of the envelope. These two little pieces the listing on eBay mentioned it supposed to be 60 millimeters so lets check how much we've actually got the long piece is little over 60 and the shorter one is about 20 which makes a little over 80 altogether Well that's a good sign they've sent me even more than I expected How about glowing in the dark? Well right away not really but let's charge it with an LED light and see what happens. Oh yea, that looks better. Well because I've ordered SB30 it is supposed to be 3 mm thick. And it is indeed very close to that. Well, as I mentioned before, I wanted to use it for my guitar, which was still a work in progress at that moment. Well, as you can see here, I've got the neck which doesn't even have the right shape yet. But I think it's the right time to install the side dots. And I want to have a standard set of dots like one one dot at 3, 5, 7, 9, and 15, 17, 19, 21 and two dots at 12 and 24 thread. So I guess I'll just take a ruler and a pencil and mark the right positions for dots. By the way this fingerboard is much thicker than a regular one. It is about 7 millimeters thick, and that's for a reason so I'll be drilling holes right in the middle of it OK I'm done here and I happened to have a drill bit which is supposed to be the right size so let's go to one of my favorite tools the drill press well you don't neccesarily need to have one to install lumen lei but I believe it's gonna be more accurate like this rather than without drill press. I'm obviously doing this for the first time and I don't want to screw anything up, so I'm very cautious about everything. Like taping the fretboard. Won't harm. Right? Or using irradius sanding lock as a support. Anyway. The most important thing at this point is using the right drill bit. For wood, not for metal or anything else. Trying to make precise job with the wrong drill bit is not fun. The whole drilling thing could be much harder if the neck was already shaped. And that is another reason why I have decided to install lumen lei at this stage. How deep to drill? Well, that's a good question. Well, I've got 80 mm of lumen ley, and I need 12 markers. 80 divided by 12 makes little over 6 mm for each. I want to have 1, maybe 1.5 mm on the top before sending down flush with the surface, and I don't really need to go deeper than 3, so I will be drilling something between 3 and 4 mm into the fretboard unfortunately, my drill bit happen to be a little thinner than the lemoine bar no big deal, I'll just sand it down a bit with the piece of sandpaper well, now is time to install the thing I will be using something like superglue but why not. I will simply put a little bit of it on a tip and well, you know, stick it in and... now you can see that I'm a little bit too optimistic about xacto tools No, it's not gonna work, luminlay is simply too hard for xacto blades I ended up using a thread cutter That worked just fine Let's speed up a little bit it's the same procedure, its pretty easy the only thing to mention here you don't want to abuse them too much while cutting And the final stage of this installation is sanding. I used a file and some sandpaper for that. Pretty easy, nothing extraordinary. Now that it's ready, let's check what it looks like IN THE DARK! A time machine just helped us to jump from a few months ago to today. Now the guitar is almost finished, and we can check what Loominee looks like on a real instrument. I have to say I'm pretty happy with the result. I've already played a couple of shows with this guitar and normally, you wouldn't even notice those markers. But they are actually charging of the stage light and once it goes off and it's completely dark, those side dots is the only thing you see. They are not too bright, but bright enough for you to know exactly where you are on the neck. And that's pretty convenient. The funny thing is I happen to have a new Ibanez guitar, RG1070, and it already comes with Lumen Lay installed. How cool is that? They are green here as opposite to blue ones on my guitar, but work in exactly the same way. Well done, Ibanez! And here comes the question. Is it worth it? For a guy like me, who only needs it for one guitar, it totally makes sense to buy it from Lumenle for 18 bucks But I guess for a manufacturer it's too pricey Considering the fact you can buy a liter of Epoxy for about 40 bucks or even as low as 10, if you happen to live in Russia and then mix it with the fluorescent powder, which is really cheap and here you have it enough lumen lei for hundreds of guitars for a price of 2 original lumen lei sets that's what I would do if I was building, let's say Ibanez guitars that is probably what they're doing anyway So, what do you think? Would you install something like this on your guitar? write it in the comments below, and don't forget to hit that subscribe button that's all for now. Thanks for watching. I'll see you soon!
